For accountants and bookkeepers

Social media for accountants and bookkeepers

Your clients don’t need more jargon. They need reminders at the right time from someone they trust. Here are the dates that matter, what to post, the rules on how you describe your firm, and how Kanosena can write your posts for you to approve.

What’s worth posting

Posts that keep you in mind when a deadline comes round.

  • Deadline reminders

    Self Assessment, payments on account, VAT and year end. Post early, then again close to the date.

  • What has changed

    New thresholds, Making Tax Digital, Budget announcements. A short, plain explanation and an offer to help.

  • Meet the team

    Who clients will speak to, and what each person looks after.

  • One service at a time

    Payroll, bookkeeping, company formation, tax returns. One clear post for each.

  • Simple tips

    Keeping receipts, separating business and personal spending, which records to keep.

  • Office news

    New starters, exams passed, opening hours over the holidays.

Your year at a glance

Self Assessment dates from GOV.UK.

31 January
Deadline for online Self Assessment returns and paying tax owed for the previous tax year, and the first payment on account. Remind people from December.
5 and 6 April
The tax year ends on 5 April and the new one starts on 6 April.
31 July
Second payment on account for Self Assessment.
5 October
Deadline to register for Self Assessment for anyone who needs to send a return for the first time.
31 October
Deadline for paper Self Assessment returns.
Making Tax Digital
Sole traders and landlords join Making Tax Digital for Income Tax based on their qualifying income in an earlier tax year: over £50,000 from 6 April 2026, over £30,000 from 6 April 2027 and over £20,000 from 6 April 2028.

Sources: Self Assessment deadlines (GOV.UK), When to sign up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (GOV.UK).

Rules worth knowing

Social media posts are advertising, so the usual rules apply. These are the ones that come up most in your line of work.

  • “Chartered Accountants” is a controlled description

    ICAEW and the other institutes have regulations on which firms may describe themselves as “Chartered Accountants”. Posts are written from your website, so they describe your firm the way your website does.

    Regulations on the “Chartered Accountants” description (ICAEW)

  • Check dates and figures at the source

    Tax dates and thresholds change. Check them against GOV.UK before a post goes out.

    Self Assessment deadlines (GOV.UK)

  • Keep public posts general

    Explain rules in general terms and invite people to get in touch, rather than telling individuals what to do in a public post.

  • Client confidentiality

    Never name a client or mention their figures without their written permission.

General information, checked on 27/11/2026. It isn’t legal advice: check with the body named for your own situation.

How Kanosena helps

You approve. We handle the rest.

  • We read your websiteWe build a short profile of your business, and every fact shows where it came from. You can edit any of it.
  • We write your weekPosts and simple branded graphics in your colours, written only from your profile, with UK dates and seasons in mind.
  • You approve every postApprove, edit, reject or ask for a new version. Only the posts you approve are scheduled.
  • We post and report backApproved posts go out to your Facebook Page, Instagram business account or LinkedIn Page, and we show you how they did.

Questions

Is LinkedIn included?

Yes. We post to LinkedIn Pages as well as Facebook Pages and Instagram business accounts. LinkedIn suits business clients, and Facebook suits local ones.

Will posts give tax advice?

Posts explain dates and changes in general terms, written from your own website, and invite people to get in touch. You approve every post before it goes out.

Can I add my own news?

Yes. You can edit any post, and the business profile we write from can be updated at any time.
